P1.evidence: No setter and no application, so P1a does not apply — the rep instead asked how the prospect found Trevor, which established the organic Instagram route. The four-part frame never ran; the open was 'I think the best way is to start from the beginning. So, yeah. What brought you here?' and no expectations were set for how the call would go. Nothing was agreed, so no frame agreement. The open question landed well: 'if you could like brief me in, like what's been going on, like what's the main thing you're trying to fix right now in terms of fitness?'

P2.evidence: Six of nine ran, several of them the best examples in the batch. The injury sequence was genuinely thorough and multi-layered — 'Did you have any other injuries that are affecting how you move or are popping up sometimes?', then 'Any other limitations that are affecting your movement or so ever?', then 'Any stiffnesses from all that sitting? I don't know, lower back, for example, or hips?' — and it surfaced the Achilles rupture, the three operations and the residual restriction with duration attached. Diet was properly interrogated rather than accepted: when the prospect said 'I eat pretty healthy' the rep pushed back with 'when you say pretty healthy, that probably can mean different things to a lot of different people' and then quantified the beers. Sleep was covered on quantity, quality, tracking, bedtime and wake time. Energy was asked. Work was established as sedentary. Against that, age arrived only because the prospect volunteered 'I am 46', height and weight were never asked, and — the gap that matters most here — health conditions, own or hereditary, were never asked at all. On a prospect with this surgical history that omission is not administrative.

P3.evidence: The two structural questions ran. The physical goal was asked directly — 'do you have, like, physical goal, and why actually you want to achieve this?' — producing the muscle, definition and spare-tire answers. The bridge ran in a good variant: 'when you think about yourself in those six months... is there anything that comes to your head that becomes possible that you've been putting off... Any projects, any dreams, sports-wise, travel-wise?' That surfaced the sauna business, and the rep followed it with 'Do you feel like that's somewhat connected to your fitness and how you feel?', which is P3e — but the prospect said 'No, not really' and the rep dropped the thread instead of working it. The deepest material on the call, the children, was supplied by the rep rather than extracted: 'Now I get it. The kids. We're doing this for the kids, not only for the sake of losing the tire.' The prospect then agreed and added the real pain himself — 'I don't have enough energy to dedicate to them' — which is exactly what P3f was supposed to produce as an answer to a question. Under the volunteered-information rule that is a miss, however well it played. The legacy drive was pursued with the 63-year-old Brazilian hiking guide story, which is good material but is the rep talking, and the reflect-back never happened. A video dropout at 00:10:26 cost the rep a question he never recovered, which is part of why this phase is thinner than it should have been.

P4.evidence: The phase was not attempted. The rep learned what the prospect used to do — gym three to four times a week, boxing, squash — but never asked what he had tried in order to fix the current problem, what happened with it, why it did not stick, or what is actually in the way. No gap was ever named. This matters commercially here: the prospect's own answer would almost certainly have been 'nothing is in the way except that I moved house and there is no gym', which is a structural obstacle the product solves outright, and it was never put on the table before the price.

P5.evidence: Only a fragment ran, and as a leading statement rather than a question: 'you want to be there for them in the long run, right? Not like in two years you're going to be, no, no, no, I'm not playing with you, I'm too old, yeah?' The prospect answered 'Yeah', which costs nothing. He was never asked what two years of no change looks like, never asked whether he would settle for it, never asked why not, and never asked to draw a line in the sand. Consequence is the phase carrying the most weight against a cash objection and it was effectively skipped for the fourth call running in this batch.

P6.evidence: The gate question ran and ran before the number: 'when we figure out all the details, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work?' The belief question — whether he thinks he can actually get there with the right structure and the right person in his corner — was never asked. And the yes he got was explicitly conditional; the prospect immediately said 'Being totally honest, I would like to understand the cost of this whole thing to see whether...' and only then 'in terms of if I'm committed to show up, yeah, I can commit myself.' That is a commitment to effort, not to proceeding. The script says move forward only on a clear yes; the rep moved forward on a qualified one and met the finance objection three minutes later.

P11.evidence: The phase applies — the rep explicitly moved to it, saying 'let's get you through the next steps. Let's talk about investment, then get you onboarded with Trevor, and we'll go from there.' Nothing in it ran. No payment, no Trevor call scheduled, no agreement, no Skool link, no questionnaire. The only thing booked was another sales call.

objection_plays.detail: Triggered twice. The first time the rep pushed back well and it worked — 'We can talk right now and you will know because I also have like a limit that I can do and what I cannot do' reopened a conversation the prospect was closing, and produced the whole financial picture. None of the scripted OA moves were used though: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'when do you make a different decision'. On the second trigger — 'I'll do a bit of numbers, and I'll drop an email and see' — the rep did not resist at all and went to the calendar.
No spouse consult was raised. His wife features only as the person who cooks.

The most complete open-wallet attempt in this batch, and still missing the piece that mattered. What ran: the isolate, cleanly worded ('apart from the finances, do you feel good about it? Is there anything else that would be stopping you from being 100% in?'); the upfront norm ('most of the guys just put it on credit card and put it up front'); the no-rough-spot reassurance almost verbatim from the manager's coaching two days earlier ('I don't want to put you in a rough spot financially... you have to put the groceries on the table too'); the custom-plans framing ('we don't have any... Everything like a set in stone. Everything is done custom'); monthly surplus, asked and then pressed for a real number ('is it more like it's $1,000 left, or $500, or $200? Because those are all different'); savings, as a hypothetical; and investments including crypto. What did not run: the permission question — 'are you comfortable having an open, honest conversation about exactly where you're at financially' — which is the exact move Chris Klevan drilled him on in the 06/30 one-to-one and the move designed to take the resistance out of everything that follows. Also missing: the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame, and the entire credit-card section (how many cards, available credit per card, used versus available). The sequence therefore went straight from 'how much is left each month' to liquidating investments with nothing in between.

A clean OD trigger that the rep elicited himself and then abandoned. He asked 'what's your timeframe on doing this renovation? When do you feel it's the more, when you will have more breathing room in terms of finances?', got 'I think in two months', confirmed 'So after summer?' — and then said 'Okay, look, let's do it like this' and moved to structuring a payment instead. Not one scripted move followed: no 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up'. Having surfaced a concrete future date on which the objection dissolves, the rep neither closed against it nor scheduled to it.
No fear or doubt about the method or the provider. He already uses Trevor's free content and rates it — 'the exercises that I've done so far have been great'.

Script gap worth logging. This prospect's blocker is a time-bound cash constraint with a stated end date roughly two months out, on a prospect who is otherwise a good fit, wants the product, already consumes the free content and raised no objection to the method. The playbook offers only win-now plays; it has no path for 'book them to start in September' and no deposit-and-hold mechanism outside the OB refund fallback. The rep's only available moves were to squeeze a payment plan out of someone who had just said he was breaking even, or to book another call. He did both. A deferred-start play would have fitted this call better than anything in the script.

notes: The discovery front half was the rep's best work in the batch — the injury and sleep questioning in particular — and then Phases 4 and 5 were skipped again, so the price landed with no root cause and no consequence behind it. The specific coaching point is the open-wallet permission question: he ran almost every other part of OC and omitted the one his manager had drilled him on 48 hours earlier, which is why the money conversation escalated to liquidating investments rather than staying comfortable.
